div.p: To overcome the drawback that switched Ethernet can not meet the real-time requirements in industrial communications, an improved message transmission model in which switch and the end-nodes control the real-time traffic with Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling was proposed. In addition, a distributed admission control method for periodic messages which is performed by the source and the destination nodes without the modification of the operational features of Ethernet switch was presented. Moreover, a more general schedulability condition for real-time periodic message over switched Ethernet was given and proved by using real-time scheduling theory.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Currently, switched Ethernet has been considered as a promising network technology for supporting real-time communications required by industrial environment. Switched Ethernet has many features for real-time communications such as provision of a large amount of bandwidth, microsegmentation of traffic, and full-duplex links. However, to provide hard real-time communications on the switched Ethernet, some real-time features must be added to both the end-nodes and the switches in order to regulate the amount of traffic on the network not to overrun the output queue of the switch [1] .

Traffic shaping techniques have been proposed in [2,3] to provide a real-time communication by limiting the amount of traffic on the network, but their methods only show that the maximum delay on the network is bounded without considering the explicit deadlines of messages.

An elastic message transmission model called FTT-Ethernet has been presented in [4] to support dynamic realtime message requirements on Ethernet. Their method uses a synchronized message transmission based on a master-slave model, where the master makes a feasible schedule for the message, and sends the schedule in TM (Trigger Message) message to the slaves. Their centralized scheme lowers the advantage of the distributed message transmission model of switched Ethernet and the master becomes a single point of failure of the network.

[5] has proposed a switched Ethernet network with support for both bit rate and timing guarantees for periodic messages. Both end-node and the switch have used EDF to schedule the transmission of real-time messages, and the switch is responsible for admission control. Only a thin layer is needed between the Ethernet protocols and the TCP/IP suite in the end-nodes which can enhance real-time communication over switched Ethernet. However, there are still some limits in the message scheduling model used in [5] as follows:

(1) The message scheduling is based on preemptive EDF algorithm, which is very difficulty to implement over switched Ethernet network; (2) The schedulability condition is based on the assumption that the deadline of a periodic realtime message is equal to its period which is not always satisfied in practice; Moreover, as for schedulability analysis for message on the reception link, it is assumed that the message are released periodically at an interval equals to its period, which is not true because of different message transmission delay from source node to switch. Therefore, the schedulbility condition given in [5] lacks of theoretical foundation.

In this paper, the limits in [5] noted above are broken through, an improved message transmission model in which switch and the end-nodes controls the real-time traffic with Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling was proposed. In addition, a distributed admission control method for periodic messages which is performed by the source and the destination nodes without the modification of the operational features of Ethernet switch was presented. Moreover, a more general feasibility condition for real-time periodic message scheduled by non-preemptive EDF algorithm over switched Ethernet was given and proved by using real-time scheduling theory.

div.head: II. NETWORK ARCHITECTURE
div.p: It is assumed that the switched Ethernet (a single switch is assumed in this paper) is running in full-duplex mode where each end-node is connected to the switch through a pair of links, i.e., the transmission link (TL) and the reception link (RL). (as shown in Figure 1). Moreover, we assume that the switch is running in store-and-forward mode and the endnodes have software (RT layer) added to support guarantees for real-time traffic by controlling traffic using EDF scheduling algorithm. Outgoing real-time message from the end-node uses UDP and is put in an EDF-sorted queue in the RT layer. Outgoing non-real-time message from the end-node typically uses TCP and is put in a FCFS-sorted (First Come First Serve) queue in the RT layer. The priority of the EDFsorted queue is higher than that of the FCFS-sorted queue, which means that the message in the FCFS-sorted queue can be transmitted only when the EDF-sorted queue is empty. In the same way, there are two different output queues for each port on the switch too (as shown in Figure 2).

div.head: III. SCHEDULING MODEL
div.p: In distributed hard real-time system, three types of messages are classified including the non real-time (NRT) message, the aperiodic real-time (ART) message and the periodic real-time (PRT) message. The priority of the PRT message is higher than that of the ART and NRT messages, while the NRT message owns the lowest priority. The main purpose of the real-time scheduling is to ensure that no PRT messages will miss their deadlines by reserving sufficient network bandwidths. The deadlines of the ART messages are statistically guaranteed, while no assurance (or best effort) is provided to the NRT messages. In this paper, we concentrate on the real-time scheduling problem of PRT messages.

div.head: A. Message Scheduling on the Source Node
div.p: The switch periodically sends synchronization messages(SYN) to the end-nodes at an interval of T SYN . In this way, every node has a uniform comprehension about global time. The resolution of the global time is T SYN . We assume that both the transmission link and the reception link are composed of a sequence of basic message transmission units called elementary cycles (ECs), and the length of each elementary cycle is T SYN (as shown in Figure 3). All of the periodic messages have their strict message transmission deadlines and the required network bandwidth should be allocated to the messages before transmission both on the transmission link and on the reception link in order to be delivered to the intended destination node within their deadlines.

In each Elementary Cycle, the scheduler in RT layer of the source Node should sort ready real-time messages in increasing order of deadline to create the queue of ready periodic messages. The scheduler guarantees that these is no transmission of the periodic messages to cross the boundary of the EC by using inserted idle time, i.e., whenever a message does not fit completely within a given EC it is delayed to the next EC (as shown in Figure 3).

div.head: B. Message Scheduling on the switch
div.p: As for the messages scheduling on the switch, the synchronization message (SYN) owns the highest priority and can preempt the transmission of other messages (as shown in Figure 4). Similarly, PRT message can preempt the transmission of NRT messages (as shown in Figure 5). Nevertheless, when a higher priority PRT message arrives at the output queue of switch just after the transmission a lower priority PRT message has started, the higher priority PRT message can not preempt the transmission of the low priority PRT message and must wait until the transmission of the low priority PRT has been completed.

When a new periodic message needs to be transmitted, it is first checked whether it can be scheduled on both the transmission and the reception links without affecting the already-scheduled messages, and a feasible schedule is made for the new message if it is schedulable. The admission control method presented in this paper is a distributed one and is performed by the source and the destination nodes.
The admission control step of a new periodic message M i from source node src i to destination node dest i which has a real-time transmission requirement M i =(C i ,T i ,D i ,R i ) is as follows.
(i) Source node src i checks the feasibility of the message on transmission link according to M i,1 (C i ,T i ,D i,1 ,R i ) and sends prt_msg_req message to dest i .
(ii) When receiving the prt_msg_req message from source node src i , destination node dest i checks the feasibility of the message transmission on reception link according to

(iii) When source node src i receives the prt_msg_rep message, it checks the message and adds the message M i in the message schedule.

Switched Ethernet provides many features for real-time communications, but it does not guarantee the timely delivery of real-time messages. This paper proposes an improved message transmission model for hard real-time communications of periodic messages on a switched Ethernet and also proposes a distributed feasibility analysis method which is performed by the source and the destination nodes without the modification of the operational features of Ethernet switch. Moreover, a more general condition for feasibility analysis for real-time periodic message over switched Ethernet was given and proved by using real-time scheduling theory.
